A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TULA research, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains appendix pages. However, v2 references missing appendices containing experimental configurations, supplementary results, ablations and reconstruction examples, limiting comparison of those aspects.

before.justification: v1 reports original membership-inference and reconstruction experiments on SST and Yelp using three language models, with numerical results in Tables 1–2 and reconstructed examples in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 reports original unlearning audits, membership-inference attacks and reconstruction experiments on SynthPAI-age and SynthPAI-inc. Results appear in Figures 2–3 and Tables 1–2, independently of the unavailable appendices.

M1.justification: v2 adds U-LiRA+, which injects mislabeled audit samples and uses shadow-model distributions. Beyond renaming TULA-black/white to TULA-MI/DR, it changes the strict attack to absolute score differences and adds a relaxed attack using per-sample classifiers over paired logits and their differences. Reconstruction replaces squared gradient-gap matching with cosine matching, embedding regularization and boundary clipping.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates sentiment classification using SST-2/SST-5 and Yelp polarity/full reviews. v2 instead reports binary age and income inference using GPT-4-generated comments in SynthPAI-age and SynthPAI-inc. Its new auditing experiments also introduce deliberately mislabeled samples, substantially changing the represented data and evaluation population.

E2.justification: v1 Table 1 compares TULA-black with LOSS and ZLIB. v2 does not retain that reported comparison: Figure 3 evaluates relaxed TULA-MI against LiRA and ULeaks, while Figure 2 introduces U-LiRA as the comparator for U-LiRA+. These are substantive changes in evaluated attack and auditing comparators.

E3.justification: v2 expands the tested unlearning procedures from gradient ascent to Retrain, GA, KL, NPO and TaskVec. Membership evaluation switches from ROC-AUC to TPR@0.1% FPR and NTS@1NFS, with new unlearning ratios and audit sizes. GPT-2 is absent from the reported evaluations, and reconstruction uses 1,000 training samples versus v1's 8,000. Missing appendices prevent comparison of all settings, but these changes are explicit.

E4.justification: v2 Table 1 visibly adds comparisons across score functions and unlearning ratios. However, its batch-unlearning tests and ablations are assigned to unavailable Appendices G and H. Reconstruction examples, shown directly in v1 Figures 2–3, are assigned to unavailable Appendix I. The extent and findings of the supplementary-analysis changes therefore cannot be reliably assessed.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly states that all experiments were independently repeated ten times. v2 describes Table 1 results as averaged but gives no visible repetition count or uncertainty intervals. Because its experimental appendices are unavailable, it is unclear whether repetition and uncertainty reporting changed or were relocated; fewer runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v1 reports TULA ROC-AUC values of 0.642–0.723 on SST/Yelp. v2 supplies new auditing and attack results, including U-LiRA+ versus U-LiRA TPRs of 17.23% versus 1.63% for GA on OPT-1.3b/SynthPAI-age in Figure 2. Reconstruction results are also replaced: Pythia's SST ROUGE-1 is 66.374 in v1, while its GA/SynthPAI-age result is 81.04 in v2. Changed tasks, methods and settings preclude interpreting these as matched performance gains.

T1.justification: v1's squared gradient-gap minimization in Definition 2 becomes a cosine-based objective with a new embedding-norm penalty and clipping constraints in v2 Equations 1–3. The white-box assumptions also change: v1 describes the unlearning procedure as unknown to the adversary, whereas v2 explicitly assumes it is known. These materially revise the mathematical formulation and assumptions, without adding theorem-level guarantees.

C1.justification: v1's central contribution is demonstrating additional privacy leakage through TULA. v2 retains that contribution but adds a second central claim: existing audits overestimate textual unlearning effectiveness, and supposedly erased texts remain detectable under worst-case auditing. The abstract, introduction and conclusion consequently cover both incomplete erasure and privacy risks from deployment.

C2.justification: v2 develops a 'false memory' explanation for weak auditing, connecting generalization and textual overlap to the need for mislabeled worst-case probes. It adds pretraining-contamination concerns and a rationale for classification-only evaluation. It also distinguishes retraining's clean erasure from privacy leakage across model releases, substantially extending v1's reference-model and reconstruction interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies full-parameter fine-tuning, reconstruction learning rates of 0.1 for Pythia and 0.45 for OPT, and regularization factor 0.1. However, dataset construction, training, unlearning and attack configurations are deferred to missing appendices. v1 directly supplies epochs, optimizer, batch size and reconstruction iteration limits. Whether these disclosures were retained, revised or relocated cannot be established, preventing a reliable overall magnitude judgment.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around exact versus inexact unlearning and population-based versus per-sample auditing. New substantive connections include Hayes et al. on U-LiRA, Aerni et al. on vulnerable audit samples, Balunovic et al. on embedding regularization, and work on KL and negative-preference unlearning. This extends well beyond bibliographic updates to v1's shorter background.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, threat-model discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 organizes the narrative around two research questions, introduces a standalone auditing section, and divides membership attacks into strict and relaxed cases. TULA variants are renamed throughout, accompanying substantial reorganization of existing prose.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1 from a wide horizontal overview into a vertical single-column diagram, adds three algorithm displays, and substantially restructures the result tables. Its Figures 2–3 are new multipanel auditing and attack plots, distinct from v1's reconstruction-example figures. Headers, typography and placement also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful worst-case auditing, additional attack comparators, exact-retraining controls and low-FPR evaluations, addressing limitations of v1's narrower experimental design. However, the review-data experiments are replaced with synthetic tasks, and crucial configurations, ablations and reconstruction examples depend on appendices absent from the supplied PDF. These verification gaps prevent reliably determining whether the substantial additions produce a net overall quality improvement.
